summary.intent: Address new automated reviewer findings that appeared on two open PRs (#634 for issue #242 and #638 for issue #246) after earlier fixes were pushed, and get both PRs to zero open findings.
summary.outcome: Fixed the JSON-mode decline message in #242 (now prints 'Initialization cancelled; nothing was written.' on stderr) and the existing-workflow note in #246 (says the workflow was kept and how to regenerate it). Dismissed the newline-filename advisory with a reason, extended tests, ran the full gate green on both worktrees, then committed, pushed, and resolved the findings.

repo: Work is split across separate git worktrees under callisto/.claude/worktrees (wp-onboarding-friction-fix for #242/#634, wp-add-inquire for #246/#638), each touching crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/init.rs and init/tests.rs.
The 'full gate' is run per worktree and sequentially, as a long-running background task, before committing and pushing.
Automated reviewer findings are tracked per PR and are resolved or dismissed by id, with a stated reason for dismissals.
Reviewer findings in this project flag advisory-level concerns, e.g. adding new permanent API for an advisory is rejected rather than fixed.

code.finding: In the #242 worktree, the JSON-mode decline path previously gave no message; it now prints 'Initialization cancelled; nothing was written.' on stderr.
In the #246 worktree, when a workflow already exists the note suggested a retry that could not work; it now says the workflow was kept and how to regenerate it.
Existing JSON decline test and existing-workflow test were extended to cover the new messages; one test needed a second edit after the first test run.

workflow: Running the full gate on both worktrees sequentially in the background avoids contention and allows waiting on a completion notification.
Fix, run targeted tests, run the full gate, then commit/push once and resolve findings together to avoid extra reviewer cycles.
Dismissing low-value advisory findings with an explicit reason is preferable to adding API surface to satisfy them.

friction: The reviewer kept surfacing new findings after each push, frustrating the user ('Still got new findings, wtf') and stretching the work over days.
A previous fix attempt repeated the 'parse Git output' mistake (in #253/#645), requiring that PR to be moved to draft.
An init test in the #246 worktree failed on the first run and needed a follow-up edit and rerun.
open_items: PR #645 (#253, Git boundary) is in draft and needs a redesign that avoids parsing Git output before further review.
The reviewer will rerun on the latest pushes of #634 and #638; results still need to be checked and reported.
